paragraphs.title: Tradition, Torah, and the Purpose of Remembrance

easy.explanation: The psalm begins, “Give ear, O my people, to my law.”
easy.q: To whom does the psalmist say, “Give ear”?

answers: The praises, strength, and wonderful works of the LORD
easy.explanation: The fathers told their children the LORD’s praises and mighty works.
easy.q: What did the fathers tell the coming generation?

answers: Make them known to their children
easy.explanation: God commanded the fathers to make His works known to their children.
easy.q: What were the fathers commanded to do with these teachings?

answers: So they would hope in God, remember His works, and keep His commandments
So they would remember only Egypt
medium.explanation: The purpose was that future generations would trust God and obey Him.
medium.q: Why were the LORD’s works to be told to future generations?

medium.explanation: The psalmist says he will open his mouth in a parable to teach old truths.
medium.q: What does the KJV word “parable” indicate in verse 2?

answers: One hopes in God and keeps His commandments; the other is stubborn and rebellious
One lives in Egypt and the other in Canaan
One is rich and the other poor
medium.explanation: The rebellious generation did not set its heart aright or remain steadfast with God.
medium.q: What contrast is made between the faithful generation and the generation in verse 8?

answers: Remembering God’s works is meant to shape a faithful future generation
Remembrance is only meant to honor ancestors
Remembrance removes the need for commandments
challenge.explanation: The testimony is passed on so future children will hope in God and obey Him.
challenge.q: How are remembrance and the future connected in this passage?

answers: Responsibility for the testimony passes from generation to generation
Only fathers may learn God’s law
The message is intended only for rulers
challenge.explanation: The passage presents an ongoing chain of teaching from parents to children.
challenge.q: What does the repeated movement from fathers to children suggest?

answers: To remember His deeds so the people will trust and obey Him
challenge.explanation: Remembering God’s works should lead to hope in Him and obedience.
challenge.q: What does “forget not the works of God” mean in context?

short_answers.question: What were the children to declare to their own children?
short_answers.answer: The works and praises of the LORD.
short_answers.explanation: Verse 6 describes the testimony being passed to another generation.

short_answers.question: What should the coming generation set upon God?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 7 says they should set their hope in God.

short_answers.question: What kind of generation were they not to become?
short_answers.explanation: This is the warning given in verse 8.

paragraphs.title: Rebellion in the Wilderness and God’s Wonders

easy.explanation: The KJV says they “turned back in the day of battle.”
easy.q: What did the children of Ephraim do in the day of battle?

answers: He divided it and led the people through
easy.explanation: He divided the sea and made the waters stand as a heap.
easy.q: What did the LORD do to the sea?

answers: Meat and a table of food
easy.explanation: They asked whether God could furnish a table and provide flesh.
easy.q: What did the people ask for in the wilderness?

answers: Forgetting His works was followed by refusing to keep His covenant
Forgetting His works caused them to build the tabernacle
medium.explanation: Verse 11 says they forgot His works, and verse 10 says they kept not His covenant.
medium.q: What connection does the psalm make between forgetting God’s works and breaking His covenant?

medium.explanation: The phrase describes sinful rebellion against God in the wilderness.
medium.q: What does “provoking the most High” mean in this passage?

answers: They continued to sin and tempt Him
medium.explanation: Even after seeing wonders, they sinned more and tempted God.
medium.q: How did Israel respond to God’s wonders?

answers: It questioned whether God could provide for His people
It described the crossing of the sea
challenge.explanation: The people had seen God’s power but still doubted His ability to supply food.
challenge.q: Why did the question, “Can God furnish a table in the wilderness?” show unbelief?

answers: God’s wonders, the people’s demand for food, and God’s anger at their unbelief
Exile, return, and the giving of the law
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from miracles to demands and then to divine anger.
challenge.q: What sequence of ideas appears in these verses?

answers: God provided and guided, but Israel did not trust Him
God did nothing, but Israel praised Him
challenge.explanation: God gave water and guidance, yet the people still demanded proof.
challenge.q: What contrast is emphasized between God’s actions and Israel’s response?

short_answers.question: What did the children of Ephraim carry?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 9 says they were armed and carrying bows.

short_answers.question: What did God use to lead Israel by night?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 14 says He led them all night with a light of fire.

short_answers.question: What did the people ask God to furnish?
short_answers.explanation: Their question appears in verse 19.

answers: Manna and the corn of heaven
easy.explanation: God rained down manna and gave them the corn of heaven.
easy.q: What did God rain down from heaven?

easy.explanation: The passage says He rained flesh and feathered fowls upon them.
easy.q: What birds did God give the people?

easy.explanation: God’s wrath came upon them and struck the chosen men of Israel.
easy.q: What followed the people’s lust and eating?

answers: God supplied food, but the people continued in lust and sin
The people supplied food, but God refused it
The people received no food and did not complain
medium.explanation: God gave manna and quail, yet the people remained unsatisfied.
medium.q: What is the main contrast in this passage?

medium.explanation: The context explains that God provided meat and feathered birds.
medium.q: What does the KJV word “flesh” refer to in this passage?

answers: Material abundance did not remove their lust or sin
medium.explanation: They were filled, but they were not separated from their lust.
medium.q: What did the people’s response after receiving food reveal?

answers: He remembered that they were flesh and did not destroy them completely
challenge.explanation: God was compassionate, turned away His anger, and remembered human weakness.
challenge.q: How is God’s mercy shown near the end of the passage?

answers: They continued to sin despite God’s works, and punishment followed
The passage connects them in no way
challenge.explanation: Verse 32 says they sinned still and believed not for His wondrous works.
challenge.q: What connection is made between unbelief and punishment?

answers: They sought Him and returned to inquire after Him
challenge.explanation: Their distress caused them to seek and remember God, though their faithfulness remained incomplete.
challenge.q: What did the people do when God slew them?

short_answers.question: What did man eat according to verse 25?
short_answers.explanation: The KJV calls the manna “angels’ food.”

short_answers.question: What came upon the people while the meat was still in their mouths?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 30 introduces the judgment with these words.

short_answers.question: What did God remember about the people?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 39 explains God’s compassion toward weak and passing human beings.

answers: God’s hand and the day He delivered them
easy.explanation: They remembered not His hand or the day He delivered them from the enemy.
easy.q: What did the people fail to remember?

easy.explanation: God turned Egypt’s rivers into blood.
easy.q: What happened to the rivers of Egypt?

easy.explanation: God smote all the firstborn in Egypt.
easy.q: What final judgment is named in this section?

answers: The people forgot God’s deliverance and again tempted Him
It caused them to keep the covenant
medium.explanation: Forgetting God’s hand led them to turn back and limit the Holy One.
medium.q: How did forgetting redemption relate to rebellion?

answers: An insect that damaged the crops
medium.explanation: The caterpiller is listed with the locust as destroying the increase of the land.
medium.q: What is a “caterpiller” in the context of the plagues?

answers: Rebellion and forgetfulness, remembrance of Egypt’s signs, and the plagues
David’s choice, Zion, and the wilderness
The giving of the law, kingship, and the sea crossing
medium.explanation: The passage moves from Israel’s rebellion to God’s signs and judgments in Egypt.
medium.q: What order of ideas appears in this section?

answers: To show that the people forgot mighty acts that had already proved God’s power
To explain the choice of Judah
challenge.explanation: The Egyptian wonders demonstrate the power that Israel had forgotten.
challenge.q: Why does the psalm recall Egypt after describing Israel’s forgetfulness?

answers: God ruled over nature and Egypt
challenge.explanation: The rivers, animals, crops, weather, and firstborn were all subject to God’s judgment.
challenge.q: What common idea is shown by the listed plagues?

answers: It repeatedly recalls God’s works to emphasize Israel’s ingratitude and forgetfulness
It says Israel physically returned to Egypt
It places the plagues in the wilderness
challenge.explanation: The return to Egypt in the narrative reinforces the charge that Israel forgot redemption.
challenge.q: What does the movement from the wilderness back to Egypt accomplish?

short_answers.question: What did God’s people turn back and tempt?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 41 says they turned back and tempted God.

short_answers.question: What did God send among the Egyptians?
short_answers.answer: Divers sorts of flies and frogs.
short_answers.explanation: These are named among the signs in verse 45.

short_answers.question: Whom did God smite in Egypt?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 51 describes the final judgment in this section.

paragraphs.title: The Exodus and Settlement in the Land

easy.explanation: He led them forth like sheep and guided them like a flock.
easy.q: How did God lead His people through the wilderness?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “He led them on safely, so that they feared not.”
easy.q: What did the people not fear as God led them safely?

answers: To the border of His sanctuary and their inheritance
easy.explanation: He brought them to the border of His sanctuary and divided the land for them.
easy.q: Where did God bring His people?

answers: Both are part of God’s continuous protection and guidance
The sea prevented entry into the land
medium.explanation: God overwhelmed their enemies at the sea and then led them to the land.
medium.q: How are the sea and the settlement in the land connected?

answers: He measured and assigned portions of land
He tied the people with a rope
He gave them a wilderness path
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the measured division of the land among the tribes.
medium.q: What does “divided them an inheritance by line” mean?

answers: He cast out the heathen before them
He made them return to Egypt
He appointed the heathen as their rulers
medium.explanation: God removed the nations and gave Israel their inheritance.
medium.q: What did God do before Israel received the land?

challenge.explanation: Israel is repeatedly pictured as a flock guided by God.
challenge.q: What image especially emphasizes God’s care for Israel?

answers: From the wilderness and sea to the holy border and tribal dwellings
From Egypt to Shiloh and then Zion
From the river to Egypt and back to the sea
challenge.explanation: The passage traces God’s guidance toward the settled inheritance.
challenge.q: What geographic movement dominates these verses?

answers: God’s guidance ended in settlement and possession of the land
The people remained without a home
The people returned to the wilderness
challenge.explanation: The tribes were established in the inheritance God gave them.
challenge.q: What does “made the tribes of Israel to dwell in their tents” imply?

short_answers.question: What overwhelmed Israel’s enemies?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 53 says the sea overwhelmed their enemies.

short_answers.question: To what border did God bring them?
short_answers.explanation: The phrase appears in verse 54.

short_answers.question: How was the inheritance divided?
short_answers.explanation: God divided the inheritance by line among the tribes.

paragraphs.title: Rebellion in the Land and the Abandonment of Shiloh

answers: They rebelled and worshipped graven images
easy.explanation: They tempted and provoked God and moved Him to jealousy with graven images.
easy.q: What did Israel do after receiving the land?

easy.explanation: The psalm says He forsook the tabernacle of Shiloh.
easy.q: What did God forsake?

easy.explanation: God delivered His strength and glory into the enemy’s hand.
easy.q: Into whose hand was Israel’s strength delivered?

answers: Rebellion, unfaithfulness, and worship of graven images
medium.explanation: Israel’s continued rebellion provoked God’s anger and rejection.
medium.q: What led to the forsaking of Shiloh?

answers: Like a bow that fails to shoot straight or hit its target
Like a bow made of wood
medium.explanation: The image represents Israel’s unfaithfulness and lack of reliable direction.
medium.q: What does “like a deceitful bow” mean?

answers: It provoked Him to anger and jealousy
It caused Him to choose David
It brought Israel safely across the sea
medium.explanation: Their high places and graven images moved God to jealousy.
medium.q: How did idolatry affect Israel’s relationship with God?

answers: Possessing the land did not guarantee faithfulness
challenge.explanation: Even after receiving the inheritance, Israel continued to rebel.
challenge.q: What does the movement from settlement to abandonment of Shiloh show?

answers: It affected the people, the sanctuary, the soldiers, and the priests
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions captivity, the tabernacle, young men, priests, and widows.
challenge.q: How extensive was the disaster described here?

answers: The disaster was so severe that even normal mourning is left unexpressed
There were no priests in Israel
challenge.explanation: The unusual silence intensifies the description of the calamity.
challenge.q: What does the statement that widows made no lamentation emphasize?

short_answers.question: What kind of bow were the people like?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 57 uses this image for Israel’s unfaithfulness.

short_answers.question: What did God forsake?
short_answers.explanation: This appears in verse 60.

short_answers.question: Who fell by the sword?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 64 says, “Their priests fell by the sword.”

paragraphs.title: The Choice of Judah, Zion, and David

easy.explanation: The psalm says He chose the tribe of Judah.
easy.q: Which tribe did God choose?

easy.explanation: He chose Mount Zion, which He loved.
easy.q: Which mountain did God choose?

easy.explanation: God took David from the sheepfolds.
easy.q: From what occupation did God take David?

answers: He smote His enemies and chose Judah, Zion, and David
He returned the people to Egypt
medium.explanation: The passage moves from judgment to God’s new choice of tribe, place, and leader.
medium.q: What did God do after the judgment connected with Shiloh?

answers: From the places where sheep were kept
medium.explanation: The phrase identifies David’s humble shepherding background.
medium.q: What does “from the sheepfolds” mean?

answers: Joseph and Ephraim were refused, while Judah was chosen
Judah was refused, while Ephraim was chosen
medium.explanation: God refused the tabernacle of Joseph and did not choose Ephraim, but chose Judah.
medium.q: What contrast is made between Joseph and Ephraim and Judah?

answers: Both are presented as central choices after the rejection of Shiloh and Ephraim
challenge.explanation: The psalm joins the chosen tribe and beloved mountain in a new center of worship.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the choice of Zion and the choice of Judah?

answers: His leadership is pictured as an enlargement of the shepherd’s task
His leadership had no connection with shepherding
challenge.explanation: David was taken from the sheepfolds to feed Jacob and Israel.
challenge.q: What does David’s movement from sheepkeeping to leadership suggest?

answers: A movement from the abandoned sanctuary to a newly chosen place and leader
A return to the plagues of Egypt
challenge.explanation: After Shiloh is forsaken, the psalm describes Zion and David as chosen.
challenge.q: What transition is presented from the tabernacle to David?

short_answers.question: Which tribe did God choose instead of Ephraim?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 68 names Judah as the chosen tribe.

short_answers.question: Which mountain did God love?
short_answers.explanation: The psalm says God chose Mount Zion, which He loved.

short_answers.question: What did David feed?
short_answers.explanation: David was brought from the sheep to feed God’s people.

answers: According to the integrity of his heart
easy.explanation: The verse says David fed them according to the integrity of his heart.
easy.q: How did David feed the people?

easy.explanation: The KJV says he guided them by the skilfulness of his hands.
easy.q: With what did David guide Israel?

easy.explanation: David is described as feeding and guiding the people like a shepherd.
easy.q: What image is used for David’s leadership?

answers: Integrity of heart and practical skill
medium.explanation: The verse joins integrity of heart with skilfulness of hands.
medium.q: What two qualities characterize David’s leadership?

medium.explanation: Integrity describes David’s sincere and upright character.
medium.q: What does “integrity of his heart” mean?

answers: The heart represents integrity, and the hands represent capable action
medium.explanation: The verse combines inward character with practical leadership ability.
medium.q: How do the heart and hands work together in the verse?

answers: He was to care for and guide the people as a shepherd cares for sheep
He was to avoid the people
He was to work only with animals
challenge.explanation: Shepherd language emphasizes care, guidance, and responsibility.
challenge.q: What does the shepherd image imply about David’s rule?

answers: It connects his shepherd background with upright and skillful leadership
It returns to the plagues of Egypt
It cancels the choice of Judah
challenge.explanation: The final verse explains the qualities of the David chosen from the sheepfolds.
challenge.q: How does the final verse summarize David’s description?

answers: The task given to David became his actual leadership of Israel
They refer to two different men
The second phrase describes Israel’s enemies
challenge.explanation: David was taken to feed Israel, and the next verse says that he did so.
challenge.q: How are “to feed” in verse 71 and “he fed them” in verse 72 related?

short_answers.question: What was the integrity of David’s?
short_answers.explanation: The verse speaks of the integrity of his heart.

short_answers.question: What guided David’s leadership?
short_answers.explanation: This phrase describes his practical ability to lead.

short_answers.question: Whom did David feed?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 71 identifies the people David was appointed to lead.
